SmartTranscripts:

Housing Committee - 2025-03-06

Meetings

  • Call to Order and Opening Remarks (00:00:10)
    The House Chair convened the Housing Committee, outlined the long agenda, and invited co-chairs and ranking members to offer opening statements.
  • HB 6889 – Evictions for Cause (Item 1) (00:05:39)
    The committee debated 'just cause' protections, adopted an oral amendment setting a 13th-month threshold, considered multiple amendments (including material noncompliance topics), and finally approved the bill by roll call.
  • SB 12 – An Act Concerning Connecticut’s Housing Needs (Item 2) (05:38:39)
    Members discussed incentives for housing production (e.g., commercial-to-residential as-of-right) and Fair Rent Commission expansion; the bill passed by roll call after extensive debate.
  • HB 5002 – Housing Concepts Study Bill (Item 3) (06:43:21)
    Described by some members as a placeholder 'dummy' bill for homelessness and affordability studies, it advanced on a divided roll call.
  • HB 7112 – Housing Omnibus (studies & pilots) (Item 4) (06:48:55)
    A multi-topic bill (including an affordable housing REIT concept, hostile architecture, and pilot programs) was JFS’d with LCO 6018; after correction, the committee revoted to adopt the substitute language.
  • Governor’s Bill 1252 – Priority Housing Development Zones (Item 5) (07:04:29)
    The Governor’s bill to incentivize local zoning reforms via PHDZs was debated and approved to the floor by roll call.
  • HB 7034 – Prohibiting Land Donation Requirement for Subdivision Approval (Item 6) (07:13:25)
    The committee advanced a bill barring mandatory land donations as subdivision conditions, citing modernized practices and housing supply goals.
  • HB 6944 – Priority Affordable Housing Planning & 8-30g Interactions (Item 7) (07:16:19)
    Debate focused on tying school construction bonuses to affordable housing, regional planning, and litigation concerns; the bill, as amended by LCO 6017, passed by roll call.
  • SB 1302 – No Eviction for Nonpayment if Online Portal Blocked (Item 8) (07:36:58)
    A narrow proposal to bar eviction for nonpayment when the landlord’s online system prevented timely payment within the grace period was approved on a split vote.
  • HB 7030 – Expanding Open Choice Voucher Pilot (Item 9) (07:42:21)
    The committee re-established and expanded a pilot allowing RAP-linked mobility for Open Choice families beyond Hartford, clarifying funding from available RAP certificates; it passed by roll call.
  • HB 7033 – Homeless Persons’ Use of Public Spaces (Item 10) (07:45:04)
    After adding exclusions for school grounds and certain DOT areas and defining daily living activities, the committee passed a bill affirming limited rights of homeless persons in public spaces with civil penalties for violations.
  • SB 1361 – Housing Growth Fund for Municipal Grants (Item 11) (08:04:50)
    Members weighed a scoring formula to reward net housing approvals and debated proof-of-construction vs. approvals; the bill, with LCO 6015, advanced by roll call.
  • SB 1364 – Tiny Homes Pilot Appropriation (Item 12) (08:30:38)
    A $10 million pilot to build up to 500 tiny homes (tied to utilities and with ongoing program design) was approved, with several members urging future affordability guardrails.
  • HB 7027 – Use of Condominium Deposits for Construction (Item 13) (08:41:26)
    The committee advanced a bill permitting escrowed condo deposits for construction when mutually agreed, as a financing flexibility to spur unit delivery.
  • HB 7110 – State-Recognized Tribes Housing & Planning; JF to Appropriations (Item 14) (08:46:22)
    The committee advanced a measure to support housing planning and studies for state-recognized tribes and adjust land management roles, sending it to Appropriations.
  • HB 6338 – Removal of Unauthorized Individuals from Real Property (Item 15) (08:51:32)
    To address unlawful occupancy, the committee approved an expedited process using an affidavit and marshal notice that triggers second-degree trespass for refusal to vacate.
  • SB 1422 – CHFA Opportunity Map Update (Item 16) (09:09:09)
    The committee approved requiring CHFA to update the statewide opportunity map used in housing finance decisions.
  • HB 6890 – Rental Assistance Program (RAP) Process Improvements (Item 17) (09:12:01)
    With LCO 6007, the bill shortened inspection and payment timelines to improve RAP lease-up speed and reduce landlord drop-off; it passed by roll call.
  • HB 6891 – Limiting Security Deposits to One Month’s Rent (Item 18) (09:23:01)
    After debate, including a failed amendment to allow voluntary excess deposits, the committee advanced a one-month cap on security deposits.
  • HB 6892 – Rent Increase Limits Upon Property Transfer (Item 19) (10:23:19)
    Members considered a one-year cap on rent hikes post-transfer (10%, with major renovation exceptions); the bill advanced following a defeated amendment attempt to tie increases to RAP max rents.
  • HB 6939 – State Funding Authorization for Right to Counsel (Item 20) (10:23:27)
    The committee approved allowing state as well as federal funds for the tenant right-to-counsel program, noting prior ARPA support and ongoing funding debates.
  • SB 1263 – Tax Credits for Converting Commercial Properties (Item 21; JFS to Finance) (10:43:30)
    A tax credit program to spur commercial-to-residential conversions, including industrial properties, was approved and referred to the Finance Committee.
  • HB 7031 – Counting ADUs in 8-30g Affordable Appeals Threshold (Item 22) (10:46:22)
    The committee advanced a bill to credit accessory dwelling units toward local affordable housing thresholds, with members flagging the need for future affordability guardrails.
